headline: PATRON REQUESTS A MEETING WITHOUT MINUTES
body: Vale asks whether the press strategy can be discussed somewhere without a receptionist. He considers this a perfectly normal request.

responses.label: Keep everything on the record
responses.hint: A paper trail, even for your own side.
responses.flavour: Vale sighs. The local paper notices the unusual openness.

responses.label: Accept his discreet invitation
responses.hint: He expects you to understand the subtext.
responses.flavour: The restaurant has no menu prices. Vale has plenty of suggestions.

headline: EVERY SUGGESTION COMES WITH PLAUSIBLE DENIABILITY
body: Vale would like an opponent embarrassed, but would prefer never to have asked. You must decide what sort of relationship this is.

responses.label: Insist on verified claims only
responses.flavour: He calls you cautious. For the moment, that is not a dismissal.

responses.label: Promise an aggressive campaign
responses.hint: The dangerous specials still require a separate decision.
responses.flavour: Vale is delighted. His lawyer is already drafting a denial of knowledge.

headline: MARINA MODEL OMITS EXISTING RESIDENTS
body: The launch display has tiny yachts, tiny restaurants and no sign of the families currently living on the site.

responses.label: Promise protected tenancies
responses.flavour: Families warm to the proposal. Vale takes an extremely long walk around the model.

responses.label: Sell the jobs story
responses.flavour: Graduates like the promised jobs. Retirees ask where the people went.

headline: NEWSPAPER ASKS WHO PAID FOR THE CAMPAIGN
body: A journalist arrives with receipts. Vale arrives with an expression that suggests you should have intercepted the journalist.

responses.label: Publish the accounts
responses.flavour: The accounts are unflattering but verifiable. The story loses its sting.

responses.label: Call the question a distraction
responses.flavour: The paper prints your phrase above a photograph of the receipts.
